title: US Presidential Determination targets recoverable rare earths
gist: A recent US presidential determination reclassifies recoverable critical minerals — end-of-life NdFeB permanent magnets, manufacturing swarf and rare-earth-bearing waste — as strategic national defence resources, giving the Department of Commerce a legal basis to restrict their export and to push domestic recovery of secondary NdPr, Dy and Tb feedstock. The full analysis sits behind a registration gate.

insights.claim: The US government is moving to treat recoverable critical minerals — including end-of-life rare-earth permanent magnets, manufacturing swarf and other waste — as strategic national defence resources rather than as ordinary industrial waste.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Reclassifying scrap as a defence resource converts a low-value waste stream into a policy-protected asset class — owners of magnet scrap and recycling capacity in the US are the direct beneficiaries.
insights.quote: The US government is moving to treat recoverable critical minerals- including end-of-life rare-earth permanent magnets, manufacturing swarf and other waste - as strategic national defence resources.
insights.locator: The US government is moving to treat

insights.claim: A recent presidential determination gives the Department of Commerce a legal basis to introduce measures that could restrict exports of recoverable critical minerals and prioritise domestic recovery.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: The legal vehicle now exists, so implementation risk is regulatory timing rather than legislation — watch Commerce rulemaking as the trigger event for scrap-flow disruption.
insights.quote: A recent presidential determination gives the Department of Commerce a legal basis to introduce measures that could restrict exports and prioritise domestic recovery.

insights.claim: For the rare-earth and magnet supply chain the US may seek to restrict exports of end-of-life NdFeB magnets, retain magnet-manufacturing scrap and swarf domestically, and limit exports of rare-earth-bearing waste to overseas processors.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Overseas processors — predominantly Chinese — that currently absorb US magnet waste face feedstock loss; the mirror image of China's own rare-earth export controls.
insights.quote: the US may seek to restrict exports of end-of-life NdFeB magnets, retain magnet-manufacturing scrap and swarf domestically, and limit exports of rare-earth-bearing waste to overseas processors
insights.locator: For the rare-earth and magnet supply chain

insights.claim: Magnet-manufacturing swarf is being treated as a policy-relevant feedstock category in its own right, implying the waste generated during magnet production — not just retired magnets — is a meaningful volume of recoverable rare earths.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Any new US magnet plant becomes a rare-earth feedstock source as well as a consumer, which changes the economics of co-locating recovery with manufacturing.
insights.locator: For the rare-earth and magnet supply chain

insights.claim: Policy could support a US-based value chain spanning magnet dismantling, demagnetisation, separation and rare-earth recovery, treating recycling as an integrated industrial capability rather than a single processing step.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Four distinct process steps means four distinct places to own capacity — separation in particular is the historic Western bottleneck and the highest-value node.
insights.quote: It could also support US-based magnet dismantling, demagnetisation, separation and rare-earth recovery
insights.locator: It could also support US-based magnet dismantling

insights.claim: The intended outcome is improved domestic access to secondary NdPr, Dy and Tb feedstock, creating a more secure supply base for US magnet manufacturing.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Heavy rare earths Dy and Tb are the tightest links in the magnet chain; a domestic secondary source would directly reduce the leverage of foreign suppliers over US magnet output.
insights.quote: improving domestic access to secondary NdPr, Dy and Tb feedstock and creating a more secure supply base for US magnet manufacturing
insights.locator: It could also support US-based magnet dismantling
